silo_relevance: This paper is highly relevant to portfolio_optimization because it directly formulates a multiperiod asset-allocation and rebalancing problem with discrete holdings, transaction costs, and market impact, then maps it to a quantum-annealing QUBO. Its main value for this silo is the explicit focus on trajectory-based portfolio construction rather than single-period optimization plus rounding.

key_points.point: Directly models multiperiod portfolio rebalancing with discrete holdings and transaction costs.
key_points.silo_note: This is the core portfolio_optimization setup: choosing asset positions over time while respecting lot-size/discrete trading constraints and rebalancing costs.

key_points.point: Incorporates permanent and temporary market impact into the portfolio objective.
key_points.silo_note: Market impact is especially important for portfolio optimization when trades are large enough to move prices, so this makes the formulation more realistic than standard mean-variance models.

key_points.point: Argues that optimizing the full trajectory can outperform solving single-period portfolios sequentially.
key_points.silo_note: For portfolio_optimization, the key claim is that a globally optimized path across time can beat period-by-period optimization followed by rounding, because it accounts for future rebalancing costs and discreteness.

key_points.point: Uses a QUBO/quantum annealing formulation to handle the discrete portfolio problem.
key_points.silo_note: This matters because the portfolio problem is cast into a binary optimization form that can, in principle, solve discrete allocation decisions directly rather than via continuous relaxations.

key_points.point: Highlights current practical limits: small solvable instances, heuristic outputs, and nontrivial encoding/embedding.
key_points.silo_note: For portfolio_optimization, these limitations mean the approach is currently more of a proof-of-concept for small asset universes and short horizons than a production-scale allocator.
